rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to observe all six compounds, locate their elution window, and identify critical pairs. The moderate temperature leaves room to tune selectivity in either direction.
Injection 1 already achieved the maximum CRF of 1.000. Shorten the gradient by one step to test a faster fully resolved method while keeping the starting composition and temperature fixed.

The shorter gradient retains maximum CRF but leaves the critical pair close to the resolution threshold. Raise temperature while holding the gradient fixed to test whether temperature improves selectivity and enables further acceleration.
At 50 C every pair remains resolved, with improved resolution for the previously critical pair. Shorten the gradient by one step to seek a faster method that preserves the maximum CRF.

Reduce the gradient slope by lowering phi1 while retaining the six-minute program, aiming to restore the critical pair to R >= 1.5. The last peak previously eluted near 0.53 organic, so 0.80 should still provide ample elution strength.

Shift the gradient window upward by 0.05 while preserving its slope to reduce retention time. This tests whether a stronger start can maintain full resolution, particularly for the early pair and the critical middle pair.

Raise the starting organic fraction another step to shorten retention, while keeping phi1 fixed so the slightly shallower slope helps protect the critical middle pair. Monitor the early pair for compression as initial retention decreases.

Continue raising phi0 with phi1 fixed to shorten the fully resolved separation while slightly reducing gradient steepness. The early pair still has resolution headroom, but its compression is the main risk.

Test one further increase in starting organic fraction to shorten elution while retaining the shallower gradient. This probes the compression limit of the early pair and the marginally resolved middle pair; injection 8 remains a fully resolved fallback.

The maximum CRF is already secured, so test a much steeper gradient for a faster, potentially reordered separation. Returning to 40 C should give the early pair more selectivity, while this run checks whether the middle pair separates again beyond its slope-dependent crossover.

Return to the promising window from injection 9 and lower phi1 one step to improve the critical middle-pair resolution. This may recover maximum CRF with a last-peak time shorter than the fastest fully resolved run so far.

Use a slightly shallower slope than injection 11 to lift the critical pair above R = 1.5, while trimming the unused high-organic end of the gradient. The last peak previously eluted near 0.49 organic, so a 0.60 endpoint should retain adequate elution strength.

Probe temperature selectivity around the fastest fully resolved method while holding the gradient fixed. Lower temperature should improve early-pair separation and will reveal whether the critical middle pair gains enough resolution to permit a stronger start or steeper gradient.

Test whether lowering temperature separates the reordered middle pair under the fastest gradient tested. Injection 10 resolved every other pair, so this isolates temperature as a possible route to a much faster maximum-CRF method.

Explore a stronger starting composition in the fast-gradient regime to shift the critical middle-pair selectivity. A temperature of 30 C may improve the late-pair resolution relative to injection 14 while preserving useful early-pair separation.

Return to the fastest well-resolved region and test a five-degree temperature increase against injection 8. This may shorten retention and improve the middle pair, although early-pair compression could set the temperature limit.

Test a modest slope increase relative to injection 8 while trimming the unused upper gradient window. This targets a slightly shorter maximum-CRF separation, with the middle pair expected to be near the resolution threshold.

Test a narrower, shallower gradient with a stronger start to recover middle-pair resolution while reducing initial retention. Use 45 C to protect early-pair selectivity; the endpoint remains above the previously estimated last-peak elution composition.

Back off one endpoint step from injection 17 to restore middle-pair resolution and increase separation margin. This should retain a compact elution window while avoiding the early-peak compression seen at phi0 = 0.30.

Use a slope between injections 12 and 19, retaining the stronger start of injection 12. This should provide more resolution margin than the fastest fully resolved method with only a small retention-time increase.

Lower the endpoint one step from injection 12 to test a compact gradient with greater middle-pair resolution margin. The last peak should still elute during the gradient, and maximum CRF is already secured by several previous methods.

Test an intermediate slope between injections 19 and 8 to seek a maximum-CRF method with more resolution margin than injection 8 and less retention than injection 19. Keep phi0 and temperature fixed to isolate the slope response.

Test whether a weaker starting composition and slightly shallower slope restore the early-pair resolution lost at 55 C in injection 16. This explores a higher-temperature, fully resolved alternative while retaining the established maximum-CRF methods as fallbacks.

Test a cooler variant of injection 21 to improve early-pair resolution while using its shallower slope to preserve middle-pair separation. This targets a maximum-CRF alternative with balanced resolution margins; injection 12 remains the fastest fully resolved method observed.

Use a slope between injections 13 and 24 at 45 C to target full resolution with less retention than injection 24. The campaign has already reached the maximum CRF; this final run tests a cooler alternative with improved early-pair separation.
